# Press Kit
Press, interview, and media inquiries: Denae, Communications (denae@opal.so)
## About Opal
Opal is the #1 Screen Time app on the App Store. We build tools that help people and families focus on what matters: less scrolling, more living. Apple Design Award Finalist. Trusted by millions of users worldwide.
Learn more at opal.so/about
## Kenneth Schlenker
Kenneth Schlenker is the founder and CEO of Opal, the free and fun app to focus better and control screen time. Opal users have saved over 500 million hours to date. Opal raised from Adjacent, Speedinvest, and founders of Duolingo, Pinterest, Mistral and more, on a mission to align computers with human well-being.
Previously, Kenneth founded and served as CEO of the online marketplace ArtList which listed $100M of inventory from collectors, auction houses, and galleries, and was acquired by artnet (FRA: ART). Kenneth trained on product and data at Google, where he worked on Maps, YouTube, and Adwords. Official headshots and portraits below, high resolution and ready for editorial use. Hover to download.

# Why Procrastination Is Detrimental To Your Life And How To Overcome It
Discover the harmful effects of procrastination on your life and learn effective strategies to overcome it.
July 13, 2023
We all procrastinate from time to time; it's part of being human. But procrastination can be detrimental if it's left unchecked. It can affect our relationships, mental health, and even our financial well being.
In this article, we'll discuss the psychology behind why we procrastinate, the consequences of procrastination, and strategies to overcome it. We'll also talk about procrastination in relation to specific mental health conditions, goal-setting, time management, and productivity.
With this knowledge, you'll be able to make the changes needed to overcome procrastination and live a better life.
‍
## Key Takeaways
- Procrastination can have a major impact on your job, grades, and life, and chronic procrastination can negatively affect mental health, social relationships, and financial well-being.
- The causes of procrastination include cognitive distortions, present bias, depression, ADHD , and different behavioral styles of procrastination, such as perfectionism, dreamer, defier, worrier, crisis-maker, and overdoer.
- Strategies to overcome procrastination include breaking tasks into smaller steps, setting deadlines, rewarding yourself for completing tasks, making a to-do list with due dates, recognizing warning signs, eliminating distractions, and increasing productivity.
- Procrastination is not a sign of laziness but is connected to mental health challenges, and overcoming procrastination requires the right knowledge, tools, and support, such as finding an accountability partner, visualizing the end result, practicing self-compassion, and using organizational strategies like time management and prioritizing tasks.
## The Science Behind Procrastination
You may be familiar with the effects and causes of procrastination, but do you know the science behind it?
Procrastination is a behavior that involves delaying a task or tasks, usually due to a lack of motivation, interest, or energy. It can have a detrimental effect on physical and mental health due to the stress and anxiety caused by procrastination.
The science behind procrastination is complex, and it is connected to the psychological concept of time management, which plays a crucial role in self-regulation. Time management can help people to manage their emotions, tasks, and energy. Poor time management can have negative consequences, such as increased stress and decreased productivity.
To overcome procrastination, it is important to understand the science behind it and to use strategies such as breaking tasks into manageable chunks, setting deadlines, and rewarding yourself for completing tasks. It is also important to identify warning signs of procrastination, eliminate distractions, and practice self-compassion.
With the right knowledge, tools, and support, you can learn to manage your time and overcome procrastination.
To learn more about the consequences of procrastination, read on.
## The Consequences of Procrastination
By continually delaying tasks, you're putting yourself at risk of serious consequences. Procrastination can lead to poor health, poor performance, negative emotions, and even health problems.
Why is procrastination bad? It can cause stress, anxiety, and even depression. It can also lead to a lack of motivation, self-doubt, and a feeling of helplessness.
Furthermore, procrastination can lead to poor time management, resulting in missed deadlines, a decline in productivity, and a lack of focus. These consequences can negatively impact an individual's physical, mental, and emotional health.
To make matters worse, procrastination can lead to feelings of guilt, shame, and regret. All of these consequences can have a lasting impact on a person's life.
Transitioning into the psychology of procrastination can help us better understand the root causes of procrastination and how to overcome it.
## The Psychology of Procrastination
We all procrastinate from time to time, but for some, it can become a major problem leading to serious physical and mental health issues. Procrastination may be a symptom of underlying psychological issues that can be detrimental to one's well-being if left unchecked.
Here are some of the ways procrastination can affect us:
- Procrastination can lead to an increase in stress levels and physical health issues such as headaches, stomach problems, and fatigue.
- Procrastination can have a negative impact on our mental health, leading to depression, anxiety, and low self-esteem.
- Procrastination can also lead to poor study habits and difficulty managing time.
- Those with ADHD and other mental health conditions may struggle with procrastination even more.
It can be difficult to find the motivation and self-control necessary to manage procrastination.
The longer we procrastinate, the more difficult it can be to break the cycle.
Understanding the psychology of procrastination is the first step to managing it and reducing its effects on our physical and mental health.
## The Cost of Procrastination
Procrastination is like a slow-burning fuse, gradually eroding away at our personal and professional lives without us even realizing it. The effects of procrastination can be far-reaching and long-lasting, impacting physical health, academic performance, job performance, and self-esteem.
Procrastination isn't only detrimental to our mental health, but it can also have serious implications for our physical health. Studies have shown that it can lead to increased stress levels, poor sleep habits, and poor eating habits. This can then lead to physical health issues such as fatigue, headaches, and depression.
In addition, procrastination can lead to poor academic performance, as students who procrastinate are more likely to receive lower grades. It can also have a negative impact on job performance, as those who procrastinate are more likely to miss deadlines and not meet expectations.
Finally, procrastination can lead to a decrease in self-esteem, as those who procrastinate may feel overwhelmed and discouraged. The constant cycle of putting off tasks can have a negative effect on our overall sense of accomplishment and self-worth.
The long-term effects of procrastination can be detrimental to our physical and mental health and can have a negative impact on our lives. Transforming our habits and taking action now can help us to break the cycle and lead healthier, more productive lives.
## Overcoming Procrastination
We understand how difficult it can be to take control of your day and break the cycle of procrastination. But it's possible to do so with the right knowledge, tools, and support.
One of the most important steps to overcoming procrastination is to make a to-do list and set deadlines. This will help you prioritize tasks and stay organized. Breaking tasks down into smaller steps can also be helpful in making them more manageable.
Additionally, recognizing warning signs and eliminating distractions is key in achieving focus. Physical health is also closely linked to procrastination. Chronic procrastination can lead to sleep deprivation, irregular eating patterns, and unhealthy regimens, all of which can take a toll on physical health.
Low self-esteem can also be a result of procrastination, as well as depression, anxiety, and poor study habits. Self-regulation plays a role in substance use disorders and other conditions that involve impulse control.
To break this cycle, it's important to practice self-compassion and be mindful of your thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Changing your mindset is the next step in the journey of overcoming procrastination.
## Changing Your Mindset
Changing your mindset is key to making progress and achieving your goals. To overcome procrastination, it's important to understand why you put things off and why it's detrimental to your physical health and overall well-being.
First, recognize that procrastination is a habit that can be broken with effort and practice. It's important to be aware of any anxiety or fear you may be feeling and to take action to address them. It might feel uncomfortable at first, but it's important to take the first step and start the task.
Allowing yourself to become overwhelmed by the task is not helpful and can lead to more procrastination. Reframing tasks into smaller, more achievable goals can help you break through the cycle of procrastination and gain momentum. Accurately assessing what you can realistically accomplish in a given time frame can help you stay focused and productive.
Finally, it's important to be gentle with yourself and keep in mind that progress is more important than perfection.
## Accountability and Support
Having an accountability partner and a supportive network can help you stay on track and make progress towards your goals. It's important to have people in your life who understand your goals and can help keep you accountable.
A supportive network provides encouragement and moral support to help you stay on track and keep going even when you feel like giving up. Here are a few ways to get started on finding an accountability partner and forming a supportive network:
- Reach out to family and friends. Ask them to check in with you regularly and provide feedback and encouragement.
- Join an online or local support group with other people who have similar goals and interests.
- Connect with a mentor or coach who can provide advice and guidance.
Having an accountability partner and a supportive network can help you stay motivated and overcome procrastination . It's important to remember that procrastination is not a sign of laziness but is connected to mental health challenges. With the right knowledge, tools, and support, you can break the cycle of procrastination and take back control of your health and well-being. The power of habits and consistency can be a powerful tool in this process.

# Unfocused and Unproductive: Why Can't I Focus?
Let's shed light on the science behind focus, explore common causes of difficulty focusing and provide techniques to improve focus.
May 31, 2023
In today's fast-paced and technology-driven world, maintaining focus has become increasingly challenging. Many of us find ourselves struggling to concentrate on tasks, constantly succumbing to distractions, and feeling unproductive at the end of the day.
If you often wonder, "Why can't I focus?" you're not alone.
This article aims to shed light on the science behind focus, explore common causes of difficulty focusing and provide techniques to improve focus.
## The Science of Focus
### Understanding the Concept of Attention
Focus is not a singular entity; rather, it encompasses various cognitive processes. Attention, a fundamental aspect of focus, involves the ability to direct mental resources toward specific stimuli or tasks while filtering out irrelevant information. It is influenced by both internal and external factors.
### The Role of Neurotransmitters
Neurotransmitters, such as dopamine and norepinephrine, play a crucial role in regulating focus. These brain chemicals or messengers facilitate communication between old and new brain cells and impact attention, motivation, and arousal levels. Imbalances in neurotransmitter levels can disrupt focus and concentration.
### The Relationship Between Focus and Productivity
Focus and productivity go hand in hand. When we can concentrate on a task without distractions, we become more efficient and accomplish more in less time. Conversely, a lack of focus or trouble focusing leads to procrastination, reduced output, and feelings of frustration.
### The Effects of Chronic Stress on Focus
Chronic stress can wreak havoc on our ability to focus. Prolonged exposure to stress hormones, such as cortisol, can impair memory and cognitive function, decrease attention span, and contribute to mental fatigue. Managing stress is vital for maintaining optimal focus.
## Common Causes of Difficulty Focusing
### Digital Distractions
The omnipresence of smartphones, social media, and constant notifications has made digital distractions a significant obstacle to focus. The temptation to check emails or scroll through social feeds can derail our attention and diminish productivity.
### Lack of Sleep
Sleep deprivation is a well-known enemy of focus. When we don't get enough restorative sleep, our cognitive abilities suffer, and our ability to concentrate declines and we have trouble focusing. Prioritizing sleep hygiene is essential for enhancing focus.
### Poor Nutrition
A balanced diet fuels our brain, and certain nutrients directly impact focus and mental energy. A deficiency in vitamins, minerals, or omega-3 fatty acids can affect cognitive function or our brain health. Optimal nutrition is vital for maintaining a sharp mind.
### Physical Environment
Our surroundings play a significant role in our ability to focus. Cluttered workspaces, excessive noise, and inadequate lighting can all hinder concentration and have a deleterious on our mental and physical health. Creating a conducive physical environment is essential for fostering focus.
### Mental Health Conditions
Mental health conditions such as anxiety, depression, and ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder) can significantly impact focus. Addressing underlying mental health concerns through therapy or medication can help alleviate difficulties in concentration.
## Techniques for Improving Focus
### Time-Blocking
Time-blocking involves allocating specific time slots for different tasks or activities. This technique helps create a structured schedule, reduces the chances of multitasking, and uses your attention span on one task at a time.
### Pomodoro Technique
The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method that involves working in focused bursts followed by short breaks. Typically, you work for 25 minutes, followed by a 5-minute break. This strategy helps maintain motivation and prevents mental fatigue.
### Mindfulness Meditation
Mindfulness meditation trains the mind to stay present and aware, reducing distractions and improving focus. Regular practice can enhance your attention span, reduce stress, and lessen any difficulty concentrating.
### Exercise
Physical exercise has been shown to have a positive impact on preventing a lack of focus. Engaging in regular exercise, whether it's cardio, strength training, or yoga, can boost focus and mental energy.
### Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) can be beneficial for combatting any lack of focus, especially when mental health conditions contribute to a lessened attention span. CBT helps individuals identify and challenge negative thought patterns that cause trouble focusing.
## The Role of Technology in Focus
### The Negative Effects of Technology on Focus
While technology can be a powerful tool, excessive use, and constant connectivity can cause us to lose focus. Endless notifications, social media scrolling, and information overload can cause trouble concentrating on important tasks.
### Ways To Use Technology To Improve Focus
Technology can also be harnessed to enhance focus. Productivity apps, focus-oriented browser extensions, and time-management tools can help us stay organized, minimize distractions, and optimize our workflow.
### The Rise of Digital Detox
Recognizing the negative impact of technology on focus, many individuals are embracing digital detoxes . Setting boundaries, unplugging from devices, and dedicating tech-free time can rejuvenate our attention span, reduce brain fog and increase productivity.
## Workplace Strategies for Enhancing Focus
### Creating a Distraction-Free Workspace
Designing a workspace that minimizes distractions is crucial for maintaining focus. Eliminate unnecessary clutter, establish clear boundaries, block website apps and optimize lighting and acoustics to create an environment conducive to concentration.
### Collaboration vs. Isolation
While collaboration is essential, striking a balance between collaborative and individual work is key. Create designated periods for intense focus and solitary work, and establish guidelines for effective collaboration to improve work performance.
### Flexible Work Schedules
Flexible work schedules, such as remote work or flextime, can empower individuals to work during their most productive hours. Allowing employees to align their work with their natural rhythms can enhance focus and productivity.
### Encouraging Breaks
Regular breaks throughout the workday are crucial for maintaining focus. Short breaks allow the brain to recharge, prevent brain fog, and promote sustained attention. Encourage employees to take breaks and provide spaces for relaxation.
## Lifestyle Changes for Better Focus
### Importance of Sleep Hygiene
Prioritizing sleep hygiene is essential for optimal focus. Establish a consistent sleep routine, create a sleep-friendly environment, and practice relaxation techniques to ensure enough rest.
### Eating Habits and Focus
Nutrition plays a vital role in cognitive function. Consuming a balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and healthy fats can support brain health and enhance focus.
### The Benefits of Physical Activity
Engaging in regular physical activity improves blood flow to the brain, releases mood-enhancing endorphins, and enhances cognitive function. Incorporating exercise into your daily routine can boost focus and mental clarity.
### How To Balance Work and Leisure
Balancing work and leisure is crucial for maintaining focus and avoiding burnout . Prioritize leisure activities that promote relaxation, hobbies that stimulate creativity, and quality time spent with loved ones.
## Navigating Distractions
### Identifying and Eliminating Distractions
Identifying the sources of distractions is the first step in combating them. Whether it's turning off notifications, setting boundaries with coworkers, or using website blockers, eliminating distractions is essential for maintaining focus.
### Techniques for Staying Focused in Distracting Environments
In distracting environments, employing techniques like wearing noise-canceling headphones, using focus-enhancing music or white noise, or practicing visualization can help maintain concentration and block out distractions.
### Managing Interruptions
Interruptions are inevitable, but managing them effectively can limit their impact on focus. Communicate your availability, set boundaries, and politely decline non-urgent interruptions to safeguard your concentration.
## When To Seek Professional Help
### Signs That Difficulty Focusing May Be a Symptom of an Underlying Condition
Persistent difficulty focusing, especially when accompanied by other symptoms such as chronic fatigue, mood disturbances, or memory problems, may indicate an underlying condition. Seek professional help if these symptoms significantly impact your daily life.
### Overview of Common Mental Health Conditions That Affect Focus
Conditions like anxiety disorders, depression, ADHD, and others can impair focus and concentration. Understanding the characteristics of these conditions can help you identify if they might be contributing to your difficulties.
### How To Find Help
If you suspect an underlying condition affecting your focus, consult with a healthcare professional. They can provide a comprehensive evaluation, offer appropriate diagnosis and treatment options, and support you in improving your focus and overall well-being.
## Beat the Distraction Trap and Reclaim Your Focus With Opal
Struggling to maintain focus is a common issue faced by many individuals in today's modern world. By implementing these techniques, it is possible to regain control over our attention and enhance our productivity and overall quality of life. So, let's take proactive steps towards sharpening our focus and toward our full potential.
Take charge of your screen time and regain focus and product
